title: Does a second laundry-hanging arm lose less if it picks a free garment instead of waiting?
summary: Two arms on one hanger-pick pile in the hanger-cell model; an arm whose choice would clash with the other arm's current pick (grasps closer than a clearance) picks the best garment that does not, and waits only if none is left. At 0.30 m blind pinching recovers 9.5 of the 28 garments an hour that blocking cost it (151 to 161), sweeping 5 (186 to 191), aiming about 1.6 of 10 (191 to 192, inside its interval). At 0.45 m nearly every pair clashes and it recovers nothing; with avoidance a third arm adds about 7.5 an hour at 0.30 m. Stylised: the clearance, the spacing time and all station times are assumed, not measured.
